To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
children and adolescents living on low incomes experience their daily lives as being stigmatized and socially excluded from their peers.
children and adolescents living under the poverty line experience social exclusion, stigmatization, and self-exclusion.
children and adolescents living under poverty conditions experience a lack of resources, which results in social exclusion and stigmatization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
children's and adolescents experiences of living in poverty and how this is connected to the practices that surround them in their daily life.
the question of whether children and adolescents living under poverty conditions are able to participate in the society in the same way as other children.
how social exclusion and stigmatization are created and reproduced through different practices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
child poverty is an expression of social exclusion, and this exclusion is a consequence of the children's and adolescents living in a social context of economic deprivation.
the social role of schools is important, not least when considering children and adolescents living on the margin.
the school is a central institution in children and adolescents lives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children and adolescents living with poverty experience a lack of social and material resources, which in turn results in social exclusion.
child poverty is a complex phenomenon that requires a holistic approach, where the school plays a key role.
the school plays an important part in the lives of children and adolescents living with poverty and the school can be a place where they feel included.
The main takeaway from our work is that
children's and adolescents experiences of child poverty are complex. It is important that social workers and other social actors working in this field are aware of
child poverty is not just a matter of material deprivation; it is also about social exclusion and segregation.
the social role of schools is crucial in order to reduce child poverty and to provide children with a sense of belonging and a sense of community.
